flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: A unit vector in C^2: |psi> = alpha|0> + beta|1> with |alpha|^2 + |beta|^2 = 1; alpha, beta are complex amplitudes.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: Measuring |psi> = alpha|0>+beta|1> yields 0 with probability |alpha|^2 and 1 with probability |beta|^2; the state collapses to the outcome.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: |psi> = cos(theta/2)|0> + e^{i phi} sin(theta/2)|1>; P(measure 1) = sin^2(theta/2). Latitude = bias, longitude = relative phase.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.q: Why must quantum gates be unitary?
flashcards.a: Closed-system evolution preserves state norm (total probability); norm-preserving matrices are exactly U with U-dagger U = I. Consequence: reversible, information-preserving.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: Global phase e^{i chi}|psi> is unobservable by any measurement; relative phase between amplitudes is observable via interference and carries information.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.q: Construct the Bell state Phi+ from |00>.
flashcards.a: Apply H to qubit 0 giving (|00>+|10>)/sqrt(2), then CNOT(control 0, target 1) swapping |10><->|11> amplitudes: result (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2).

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: Assume factorisation (a0,a1)x(b0,b1): equations force b1=0 then a1=0, but component |11> needs a1*b1 = 1/sqrt(2) != 0. Contradiction: not separable.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.q: Memory cost of an exact n-qubit simulation?
flashcards.a: 16 x 2^n bytes (complex128 per amplitude): 30 qubits ~17 GB, 40 ~17 TB, 50 ~18 PB. Exact simulation caps out around 45-50 qubits.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: No. Each side's local statistics are 50/50 regardless of remote actions (reduced density matrix = I/2); correlations appear only after classical comparison. No-signalling theorem.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.q: Operational test distinguishing superposition from a classical 50/50 mixture?
flashcards.a: Apply H then measure: (|0>+|1>)/sqrt(2) returns 0 deterministically (interference); a classical fair coin stays 50/50 under any 'rotation'.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.q: What does no-cloning forbid and why?
flashcards.a: Copying unknown |psi> -> |psi>|psi> is nonlinear in amplitudes, but quantum evolution is linear, so no physical device can clone arbitrary states. Known classical descriptions are fine to copy.

flashcards.topic: Qubits, Superposition, Entanglement, the Bloch Sphere
flashcards.a: Reshape 2-qubit amplitudes into a 2x2 matrix A with c_ij = amplitude of |ij>; the state factors iff rank(A) = 1.
